purpose: Cross-language contract for the #1099 single-rate tax resolution chain. Cloud (backend/app/Services/Customer/TaxResolver.php) is AUTHORITATIVE; the workstation mirror (workstation/internal/service/tax_resolver.go) must reproduce it to the yen so an offline line stamps the rate Cloud would have stamped. This file is byte-identical in both repos: backend/tests/Fixtures/ and workstation/internal/service/testdata/. Edit both or the digest check fails.
chain: tier 2  section in this menu      MenuMenuSection.tax_type_id   (#1218)
none    -> rate 0, NO snapshot   (legacy tax_rate fallback was dropped in plan-043 T6.2)
tier_collapse_note: The workstation never sees tiers 1-4 separately: the menu feed collapses them into one column (menu_items.tax_type_id) at backend/app/Services/Customer/CustomerMenuService.php — $menuProduct->tax_type_id ?? <section-in-this-menu> ?? $menu->tax_type_id ?? $product->tax_type_id (#1218 added the middle two; they sit ABOVE the product by ruling, so a menu-wide 8% does override a tax-exempt product). Each case therefore states both inputs; the Go harness applies exactly that collapse, and a case where the collapse itself would lose information is a bug in the feed, not in the resolver. The collapse order is pinned on the Cloud side by tests/Feature/Customer/MenuFeedTaxCollapseTest.php.
digest_algorithm: sha256 over the lines produced by joining, per case in file order, the fields name|menu_tax_type_id|product_tax_type_id|branch_default_tax_type_id|legacy_branch_tax_rate|expect.tax_type_id|expect.rate|expect.has_snapshot with '|', absent ids rendered as '~', rates formatted with exactly 2 decimals, booleans as 'true'/'false', cases joined with '\n' (no trailing newline).

cases.name: tier1 menu override wins over the product type
cases.why: This is how takeaway gets 8%: the takeaway MENU carries the reduced type on its line. No order-type input exists anywhere in the chain.

cases.name: tier1 menu override wins even when it is the more expensive rate
cases.why: Precedence is positional, not min/max. A resolver that picked the lower rate would pass the case above and fail this one.

cases.name: tier2 product type applies when the menu line overrides nothing
cases.why: The product's own type must beat the branch default.

cases.name: tier3 branch default applies when neither line nor product carries a type
cases.why: A shop-wide default, e.g. an all-takeaway branch.

cases.name: tier4 brand default applies when the branch has no default either
cases.why: STANDARD is the brand's is_default row. The legacy 8 is deliberately different so a resolver that fell back to it fails here.

cases.name: explicit 0% EXEMPT is a stamped rate, not an absent one
cases.why: 非課税 must be distinguishable from unresolved: same rate, but has_snapshot true and a type id to print on the invoice.

cases.name: nothing resolves anywhere - 0% and NO snapshot, legacy rate is NOT used
cases.why: Only reachable for a brand with zero tax types (seeding skipped). Cloud dropped the legacy tax_rate fallback in plan-043 T6.2, so the workstation must not resurrect it: a 10% offline receipt that Cloud re-prices to 0% is a receipt handed to a customer that the books then contradict. THIS CASE REQUIRES no_brand_default.

cases.name: an INACTIVE type still resolves when explicitly assigned to the line
cases.why: Deactivation blocks NEW assignment (BR-TT02); it does not retroactively unstick lines that already point at the type. Filtering is_active inside the resolver would silently re-rate live menus the moment an admin deactivates a type.

cases.name: an INACTIVE type still resolves as the branch default
cases.why: Same rule one tier down. Cloud follows ShopOrderSetting.default_tax_type_id without an is_active filter, so the mirror must not add one.

cases.name: a branch default pointing at a type that does not exist falls THROUGH to the brand default
cases.why: On Cloud the FK cannot dangle, so this is the OFFLINE-ONLY case: the workstation pulled shop_settings before the tax_types row arrived. Continuing down the chain keeps the tier order; bailing out to the legacy rate would stamp 8 where Cloud stamps 10.

cases.name: a menu line pointing at a type that does not exist falls THROUGH to the branch default
cases.why: Same partial-sync window, one tier up. Cloud reaches this state via a soft-deleted type, whose relation resolves to null.

cases.name: a fractional rate survives the round trip unchanged
cases.why: rate is DECIMAL(5,2) on Cloud and REAL in SQLite. A mirror that rounded to an integer percent, or that lost the .25 through a float32, would diverge on every Vietnamese line.
